subject: Clarify: penetration testing scope for private VPC deployment and credentialed access
messages:
From: Alice Morrison <alice.morrison@maplebank.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Pen testing details for private deployment - scope & evidence request

Jonas —

Thanks for taking this. We’re preparing our third-party assessment ahead of a production integration with Redwood’s private deployment option. Our security team needs: 1) a redacted penetration test report (most recent), 2) a clear statement of the deployment boundary for customer VPC / on-prem installs, and 3) remediation evidence for any medium-or-higher findings from the last test.

Two specific questions from our SecOps:
- Do Redwood-managed nodes in a Private/VPC deployment ever have public IPs, or are they strictly peered/private interfaces?
- Will you permit credentialed (authenticated) testing against host-level services (SSH/RDP) for customer-scoped tests, or is host access out-of-scope?

We also need to confirm whether KMS/HSM key material ever leaves the customer-managed network and what the access model looks like.

Can you reply with the redacted report and a one-page boundary summary by EOD Tuesday? We have an external vendor (RedTeam Labs) who will run the test but they require the scope matrix and a contact at Redwood.

Thanks,
Alice Morrison
Senior Security Engineer, MapleBank
secops@maplebank.com

Attachment: (requested) pentest scope template - we will populate once scope confirmed
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morrison <alice.morrison@maplebank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pen testing details for private deployment - scope & evidence request

Alice —

Appreciate the clear ask. Looping in Evelyn (security) and Dev (solutions) to provide the technical boundary and remediation artifacts. Quick answers up front:
- Redwood never assigns public IPs to nodes that host customer data in private deployments; connectivity is via customer-controlled peering or private links.
- By default, host-level access (SSH/RDP) is out-of-scope for vendor testing. We support credentialed testing at the application/API layer and can provide ephemeral test service accounts for more in-depth checks if the customer signs an access addendum.

I’m attaching a redacted summary of our latest internal pen test and a network boundary diagram to start. Evelyn, can you confirm the remediation status for medium-or-higher items and whether we can accommodate credentialed host testing under an addendum? Also, please populate the scope matrix for the RedTeam vendor.

Next steps: 1) Evelyn to confirm remediation + provide evidence, 2) Dev to add required service-account provisioning steps, 3) Laura to coordinate contracting addendum if needed.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_pen_test_summary_2026Q2_redacted.pdf, network_boundary_map.svg
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Morrison <alice.morrison@maplebank.com>
Date: 2026-07-21T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pen testing details for private deployment - scope & evidence request

Team / Alice —

Thanks for the heads-up, Jonas. Internal summary and clarifications below; I’ve attached the remediation evidence and a populated scope matrix for RedTeam.

1) Boundary assumptions (private deployment):
- Customer VPC is the authoritative network boundary. Redwood components are deployed into the customer VPC (via a PrivateLink/peering model) or into a customer-managed subnet when on-prem packages are used.
- We do not assign public IP addresses to compute nodes that store customer data. Network egress is through customer-controlled NAT/firewall unless explicit routing is requested.
- Host-level maintenance access is via a management plane that uses ephemeral, mutual-TLS authenticated channels; the management plane is on a separate control network and does not expose SSH/RDP to the customer VPC.

2) Credentialed testing:
- Standard practice: vendor tests are authenticated at the API/application layer using scoped service accounts. Host-level (SSH/RDP) credentialed tests are considered out-of-scope except under a strict addendum: vendor must use ephemeral accounts issued by the customer, testing window scheduled, access logged to an immutable audit trail, and remediation SLAs agreed. We are willing to support this if MapleBank signs the addendum and coordinates with our ops team.

3) Remediation status (last internal test Q2 2026):
- One medium finding (temporary metadata exposure via misconfigured IMDS-like endpoint) 1 resolved on 2026-06-15; evidence attached (kms_key_access_evidence.pdf).
- Two low findings (informational) addressed and tracked in our backlog with mitigations deployed.

4) KMS / key material handling:
- Customer-managed keys can be used via an external key encryption mechanism; key material never leaves the customer network in cases where HSM-backed keys are required. Access to key operations from Redwood components is performed via audited, least-privilege IAM roles and ephemeral credentials; we provide logs as part of SOC 2 evidence.

5) In-scope endpoints for vendor testing (recommended):
- Public-facing admin/API endpoints (if customer exposes them through their NAT)
- Ingress load balancers assigned to the customer VPC
- Internal application endpoints reachable over peering (subject to approved test IP ranges)

I attached: pentest_scope_matrix.xlsx (populated), kms_key_access_evidence.pdf (redacted evidence), and a more detailed network_boundary_map.svg.

If MapleBank wants host-level credentialed tests, please confirm and we will draft the addendum (contract + operational playbook). Otherwise, RedTeam can proceed with the documented application-layer scope.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.com

Attachments: pentest_scope_matrix.xlsx, kms_key_access_evidence.pdf, network_boundary_map.svg

Subject: Re: Pen testing details for private deployment - scope & evidence request

Evelyn / Jonas / Laura —

Appreciate the thorough reply and the artifacts. The remediation evidence and scope matrix look good. MapleBank will proceed with application-layer and ingress testing only; we will not request host-level credentialed tests at this time. RedTeam is copied and will initiate scheduling.

Requested next steps from Redwood:
- Please confirm a single point of contact in ops for test day coordination (port openings, temporary test IP ranges, emergency rollback contact).
- Provide the signed scope matrix / addendum acknowledging the boundary assumptions (we can use DocuSign link).

Jonas / Laura: can you confirm ops contact? If we get that today we can book RedTeam for the week of Aug 3.

Thanks,
Alice Morrison
Senior Security Engineer, MapleBank
secops@maplebank.com
